name: Qualitative or Quantitative Defects of Beta-Sarcoglycan

criteria.description: Progressive proximal muscle weakness predominantly affecting limb-girdle muscles
Reduced or absent beta-sarcoglycan protein expression on immunohistochemistry of muscle biopsy
Identification of pathogenic variants in the SGCB gene encoding beta-sarcoglycan

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of progressive proximal muscle weakness with either muscle biopsy showing reduced beta-sarcoglycan or identification of pathogenic SGCB variants
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is confirmed by genetic testing and muscle biopsy findings; clinical presentation supports diagnosis.

searchTerms: gradual weakness of shoulder and hip muscles

pathognomonic.symptomName: Marked reduction or absence of beta-sarcoglycan protein in muscle tissue
searchTerms: lack of specific muscle membrane protein

common.symptomName: Muscle atrophy predominantly in shoulder and pelvic girdle muscles
searchTerms: muscle wasting in shoulder and hip areas
loss of muscle bulk near trunk
muscle disease changes on EMG test

common.symptomName: Difficulty climbing stairs or rising from a seated position

searchTerms: heart muscle disease with weak left ventricle

occasional.symptomName: Respiratory muscle weakness leading to restrictive lung disease
searchTerms: breathing difficulty from weak chest muscles
calf muscles appear enlarged but weak
spine curvature due to weak muscles
muscle weakness causing sideways spine bend

imaging: Muscle MRI showing fatty replacement and muscle atrophy in proximal limb muscles
genetic: Pathogenic variants in SGCB gene (beta-sarcoglycan gene)
other: Muscle biopsy demonstrating reduced or absent beta-sarcoglycan protein by immunohistochemistry

distinguishingFeatures: Mutations in SGCA gene instead of SGCB
Similar clinical presentation but different genetic etiology
Caused by mutations in CAPN3 gene
Typically earlier onset and different muscle biopsy findings

redFlags: Rapidly progressive proximal muscle weakness in childhood or adolescence
Markedly elevated serum creatine kinase levels (>10x normal)
Evidence of cardiomyopathy or respiratory insufficiency
references: Nigro V, Savarese M. Genetic basis of limb-girdle muscular dystrophies: the 2022 update. Neuromuscul Disord. 2022;32(6):523-534.
Orphanet: Qualitative or quantitative defects of beta-sarcoglycan. ORPHA:207063.
Bushby K, et al. Diagnosis and management of limb-girdle muscular dystrophies: consensus statement. Neuromuscul Disord. 2014;24(4):289-302.
